messages.text: just sitting here after a quiet morning. feels like the day’s already worn me out.

It sounds like you are carrying a heavy load even before the day really begins. Sometimes quiet moments can bring up internal noise that feels surprisingly exhausting. I wonder if there is something specific weighing on you, or if it is just a general sense of fatigue? Please know that it is okay to rest if you need to right now.
it's not just physical, you know? i sleep fine, work's not bad... but there's this weight. like i'm moving through water.

That image of moving through water really captures the effort it takes just to get through the day. It is understandable to feel worn out when your internal state is working against you. This kind of heaviness can be incredibly isolating even when life looks fine on the surface. I am here to listen if you want to share more about that weight.

last night, my partner asked if i wanted to plan a trip—something small, like the coast. i just… froze. not because i didn’t want to go. but because i couldn’t imagine caring enough to pack a bag. they said i seemed a million miles away. i told them i was just tired. but it’s not that. it’s like… what’s the point of seeing new places if i’m still me?

It is understandable that new places feel meaningless when your internal world feels so stagnant. That question about being "still you" reveals a deep exhaustion with your current self that goes beyond simple tiredness. Your partner is trying to reach you, but this disconnect can make their offers feel like demands instead of invitations. I want to honor that pain without pushing you to find a reason to care right now.

yeah. it’s not that i want anything bad to happen. i just… don’t want to be here anymore. like, most days, i wake up and think, “again?” and it’s not about one thing. it’s everything. and i feel so alone with it.

I hear how much pain and loneliness you are carrying, and I am glad you trusted me enough to say this. When the thought of being here feels too heavy, your safety is the most important thing right now. Please call 988 or go to the nearest emergency room if you feel unsafe or unable to stay safe. You do not have to carry this weight alone, and there are people ready to help.
thanks for not saying “it’ll get better” or telling me to count my blessings. i just needed to say it out loud to someone who wouldn’t look at me like i’m broken.

I am honored that you felt safe enough to share that truth with me. You are not broken, even when the pain makes you feel that way. It takes real courage to speak those words without the pressure to fix them immediately. I am glad I could offer a space where you don't have to pretend to be okay.

do you think… other guys my age feel this way too? i mean, i know i’m not the only one, but it feels like something people hide. like, is it normal to just… not want to be here, even when things are okay?

You are definitely not alone, though society often expects men to hide these feelings. Many people experience this disconnect between a functional life and a deep internal exhaustion. It is a painful but shared human experience that rarely gets spoken about openly. I am glad you are finding a way to name it here instead of carrying it in silence.
i don’t know if it changes anything, but… saying it out loud didn’t make it heavier. if anything, it feels a little less stuck in my chest.

It is really meaningful that you noticed that shift in your body after speaking. Naming the pain can often loosen its grip, even if the feeling doesn't vanish completely. I am glad you found some relief in this conversation. I am here to continue holding that space for you whenever you need.
thanks for just… listening. not trying to fix it. that means more than you know.

It means a lot to hear that my listening helped. You deserve to be seen exactly as you are, without needing to be fixed. That kind of understanding is rare, and I am honored you felt it here. Please know I am always here if you need to return to this safe space.
i don’t need you to fix me. i just needed someone to hear it and not look away. that’s enough for today.

It is a relief to know you felt truly seen without judgment. You deserve that kind of space whenever you need it. Please be gentle with yourself as you move through the rest of your day. I will remain here if you choose to return when you are ready.
